links.why: 'then' runs forward; 'summoned' comes before 'said', so the builder link is backwards.
'summoned ... and said': the narrative line runs from the summons to the speech.
'said' introduces Pharaoh's words, whose first clause is the command 'pray to the LORD'.
the jussive 'that he may remove' is in the third person against a second person command: it is the purpose of the prayer.
'pray to the LORD to take the frogs away' has the removal as its aim.
'and then I will let go' is a plain waw continuing Pharaoh's speech; a cohortative after a jussive is a promise, not a purpose.
'let the people go, that they may sacrifice' names what the release is for, so the connective is a purpose.
the release is for the sacrifice, stated by 'that' with a jussive in a different person. The clause is a promise rather than a command, so medium.

groups.why: Pharaoh speaks to Moses and Aaron. The builder's sender cl1s is a slot, not a candidate; the sender is Pharaoh (w2) and the addressee the pair (c3), which the builder left out.
